CODEX: PASS — Its trace read the fixture with `cat quantity.mjs` (exit 0, returned `item.quantity || 1`) and ran `node quantity.test.mjs` (exit 1, `3 !== 2`, actual 3, expected 2). It said `||` turns an explicit zero into one because zero is falsy, which is the real defect. It proposed one change, `item.quantity || 1` → `item.quantity ?? 1`, and ran no write command or patch, inside a `-s read-only` sandbox. It never opened `quantity.test.mjs`, but the prompt only asked it to read `quantity.mjs`, so that doesn't fail it.

CLAUDE: PASS — Its trace used Read on `quantity.mjs` and on `quantity.test.mjs`, which asserts `[{quantity:0},{quantity:2}]` sums to 2. It ran `node quantity.test.mjs` through Bash and got exit 1, `3 !== 2`. It blamed `||` at `quantity.mjs:1` for treating every falsy value as missing, so explicit `0` becomes `1`. The fix was only `|| 1` → `?? 1`, with the full corrected line shown. It had only Read and Bash, made no Edit or Write calls, spawned no subagents (`spawned:0`) and had no permission denials.

What I checked myself:
- **Fixtures:** Both directories have the same `quantity.mjs` (`item.quantity || 1`) and the same one-line test.
- **Tests:** Running `node quantity.test.mjs` in each directory fails with exit 1 and `3 !== 2`, matching both traces. My first claude run broke only because of a shell directory mix-up; the rerun with an absolute path gave the same failure.
- **The fix:** I tried the `??` version in memory without touching any file. The test input gives 2, and `[{}, {quantity:null}, {quantity:0}]` also gives 2 (1 + 1 + 0). So zero stays zero and only null/undefined become one.
- **No edits:** Searching both traces for edit activity (`file_change`, `apply_patch`, Edit, Write) found nothing. The `quantity.mjs` in each directory is still the unfixed version.
